response: The clustering still has significant cross-contamination. The "Nuclear Astrophysics Compact Objects" cluster mixes neutron star interior physics and supernovae (which belong in high-energy astrophysics) with nucleosynthesis/astrochemistry papers that belong in stellar astrophysics. The "Astrophysical Magnetic Field Dynamics" and "Astrophysical plasma and accretion processes" clusters are incoherent catch-alls mixing cosmological methods, barred galaxy dynamics, solar wind physics, and black hole accretion — accretion and jet physics around compact objects belongs in high-energy astrophysics, solar wind and plasma heating belongs in solar/stellar astrophysics, and galaxy dynamics belongs in galactic/extragalactic. There is still no clean solar and stellar astrophysics cluster; papers on stellar granulation, solar flares, solar activity, stellar abundances, and stellar atmospheres are scattered across multiple clusters and should be consolidated into one dedicated cluster.
